title: Tenant hotkey fanout and TTL orchestration for embedding cache
creator: Maya Chen
description: Scope: Implement a tenant-aware hotkey fanout and unified TTL orchestration layer for the embedding cache to improve P95 latency, reduce tail cost, and control deduplication collision rates. This ticket covers: detection of tenant 'hot prefixes' (repeated queries/prefixes within a tenant), a fast-path fanout that routes hotkey lookups to dedicated in-memory shards, a compact content-fingerprint dedupe layer using 64-bit XxHash for canonicalization, and a tenant-scoped TTL harmonizer that reduces cache churn while keeping invalidation predictable. The goal is to increase embedding cache hit rate for high-volume tenants by 20% (measured on realistic traffic profiles) and reduce P95 embedding endpoint latency by 25ms on average for cached requests, without increasing false-positive dedupe collisions beyond 0.1% for production traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Architecture implemented and reviewed: hotkey detector, fanout routing, tenant shard mapping, fingerprint dedupe, TTL harmonizer
Integration tests that simulate mixed QPS tenants show >=20% improvement in overall cache hit-rate for identified hotkeys compared to baseline
Latency: end-to-end P95 for embedding calls hitting cache reduced by >=25ms in canary traffic
Collision rate for dedupe (measured by offline ground-truth) <= 0.1% for sample production dataset
No quality regression for reranking/embedding-dependent features (sanity evals pass on designated prompt set)
Canary rollout plan exists and feature gated behind runtime-1.19 feature flag; smooth rollback path documented
technical_notes: Hotkey detection: sliding-window QPS per tenant+prefix (1m/5m) with an entropy score to avoid accidental spikes; hot threshold configurable via console
Fast-path fanout: route hotkey lookups to dedicated in-memory shards (smaller footprint, low-latency local cache) using rendezvous hashing keyed by tenant_id to keep affinity stable under rebalancing
Fingerprinting: compute UTF-8 normalized content then XxHash64 -> use 64-bit fingerprint for in-cache key. Maintain optional Murmur3 fallback for cross-platform parity during transition
Deduplication: tenant-cohort Count-Min sketch to prefilter likely duplicates, followed by exact fingerprint lookup to avoid extra vector encodings
Negative cache: per-tenant rotating Bloom filters (epoched every TTL-window) to avoid expensive misses for recently observed negatives; supports rapid negative response for common prefixes
TTL harmonizer: dynamic TTL buckets (10s, 1m, 5m, 1h, 24h) assigned by prefix entropy and observed QPS; long-tail prefixes default to short TTLs to prevent stale embeddings
Invalidation: versioned content-signature produced by normalization pipeline; publish invalidation events to Kafka topic embed-cache-invalidate for reactive eviction across shards
Eviction policy: hybrid LFU-LRU with percentile anchoring (avoid evicting top 5% freq keys), tenant-aware size caps and soft eviction signals to platform orchestrator
Shard migration: use a reindexing window with double-write during shard moves and rendezvous-hash migration TTL to avoid cold misses
Observability: new dashboards for per-tenant hit/miss, fingerprint collision counts, false-positive audit sampling, and fanout latency breakdown
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged runtime rollout in runtime-1.19: start with deterministic canary on internal tenants (10%)
Phase 1 (Canary): internal + opt-in external tenants, monitor hit-rate, P95 latency, and collision metric for 72 hours
Phase 2 (Gradual): increase to 30% of production requests over 7 days if metrics stable; enable tenant-scoped override from Console
Phase 3 (Full): enable by default for all tenants with ability to opt-out per-tenant for 30 days; document rollback: disable feature flag and drain fanout shards by TTL window
Emergency rollback: disable fanout routing and invalidate fast-path cache entries; fallback to global embedding cache path
testing_plan: Unit tests for normalization -> fingerprint pipeline, verifying canonicalization across unicode whitespace and punctuation variants
Deterministic integration test that replays production traces with and without fanout to measure hit-rate delta
Load test with synthetic hotkey tenants at 10k RPS to validate shard saturation and kv-cache latency under stress
Collision audit: run offline comparison between 64-bit fingerprint collisions and full-payload exact-match to quantify false positive rate
Chaos tests: simulate Kafka invalidation lag and verify coherent eviction semantics across shards
E2E quality eval: run existing reranking prompt set to detect any embedding quality regressions after canonicalization changes
